title: Senior Engineering Technician
description:
Primary Function of Position:

This position will be responsible for supporting the Manufacturing Engineering team, which includes upgrade, troubleshooting, repair, test, and calibration. This also requires system technical depth, experience, and independent decision making, and demonstrates competency to perform the duties of a Senior Engineering technician. Ability to coordinate system repairs with other engineering disciplines to limit down time.

Candidates must be highly motivated with a strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required as well as a commitment to high product quality.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate activities with engineers and line supervisors to make sure that each system is in good working order.
  • Perform quick triage of the issue and recommend best course of action to limit downtime.
  • Perform simple reworks on the spot (cable crimping, solder components, tap threads, clean optics, adjust alignments etc.).
  • Document all activities in support for our formal records.
  • Order parts and assemble/bring up duplicate fixtures for production.
  • Assist or execute engineering level tests and collect data to support design of experiment activities or characterize an assembly.
  • Assist with parts order, build, and modification of development fixtures for evaluation.
  • Generate or assist on the implementation of Engineering Change orders.
  • Follows all corporate, safety, SOP, DOP procedures and regulations.
  • Understands problems, areas of risk, and areas for improvement within work unit, including the processes and procedures.
  • Perform other engineering technician duties as needed.

Skill/Job Requirements:

  • Significant experience with wiring diagrams, schematics, assembly drawings, fab drawings, mechanical drawings.
  • Ability to perform complex technical issues on various electrical/electro-mechanical assemblies.
  • Working knowledge of computers, word processing and spreadsheet applications for documentation and data presentation.
  • Ability to read, modify, and execute test scripts use for debug
  • Ability to learn quickly and adapt to variety of technologies that allow effective troubleshooting. Examples: Digital and Analog Electronics components, optical components, servo components, machined parts, sheet metal parts, cable assemblies.
  • Good communication skills, verbal and written, to be able to partner effectively with production techs, supervisors, training department as well as Manufacturing/Design/Test Engineers.
  • Proven ability to work well in team environment
  • Experience with JIRA, Agile, and SAP or equivalent tools
  • Effectively use of troubleshooting and measurement equipment like oscilloscopes, multimeters, function generators, custom test platforms.
  • Document findings of investigation in quality notifications which are part of official Device History Records.
  • Electronic and Mechanical assembly skills (Examples: soldering, crimping, box build, fiber handling, optical component handling, cable routing, and use of RTV/epoxy).

Education/Experience:

  • AS degree, trade school, military technical training. B.S. EE/Comp E or equivalent is preferred.
  • A minimum of eight years of troubleshooting experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Who we are

Neros is a defense technology company rebuilding America’s drone industrial base. We design and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are tested in combat, iterated at startup speed, and built at massive scale. Our team culture is fast, hands-on, and obsessed with closing the gap between design and deployment.

As drones transform the character of warfare, Neros is delivering the systems the West needs to compete on the modern battlefield and deter the adversaries of democracy. We’re hiring engineers, operators, and builders who want to move fast, take on extreme ownership, and get capability into the hands of warfighters in months, not years.

What you will be doing

The Technical Project Manager will support the technical planning, cost analysis, resource planning, and execution tracking for RDT&E, engineering, and program related efforts supporting defense programs. This role will work closely with Program Management, Engineering, Finance, Contracts, Manufacturing, Test, and other functional teams to develop detailed estimates, resource plans, technical schedules, and cost forecasts necessary to support program execution. The Technical Project Manager will provide visibility into the cost, resource, and schedule impacts of technical activities while helping cross-functional teams maintain alignment against established program objectives.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain detailed cost, schedule, and resource plans for engineering and RDT&E efforts, including labor/FTE requirements, materials, prototype hardware, testing, tooling, equipment, software, travel, and other project needs
  • Develop and maintain technical project schedules that capture milestones, dependencies, resource constraints, testing and qualification activities, and required completion dates
  • Develop cost estimates, budgets, forecasts, and budget-versus-actual analysis for assigned technical efforts, including visibility by Delivery Order, CLIN, work package, or other applicable level
  • Develop Basis of Estimates (BOEs) and supporting cost and resource inputs for proposals, Delivery Orders, contract modifications, and new technical scope in coordination with Engineering, Finance, Contracts, and Program Management
  • Track technical workstreams against established cost, schedule, and resource plans, identify variances and constraints, evaluate impacts from changing requirements or scope, and communicate risks, forecasts, and required actions to cross-functional stakeholders

You should have the following

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Project Management, Finance, or a related technical or quantitative discipline; or 4–8 years of relevant professional experience in a related field in lieu of a degree
  • Experience supporting or leading engineering development, R&D/RDT&E, testing, qualification, production, or other technical development activities
  • Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining detailed project schedules, including milestones, dependencies, resource requirements, and schedule tracking
  • Demonstrated experience developing labor/resource estimates, project budgets, cost forecasts, or other quantitative project plans
  • Experience tracking cost, schedule, and resource performance and identifying or communicating variances, constraints, and forecast impacts
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including experience developing and maintaining cost, resource, budget, or forecasting models
  • Experience with Microsoft Project or another project scheduling/planning tool
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering and other technical or operational teams to develop plans and support execution

Nice to Have

  • Experience within aerospace, defense, robotics, UAS, space, or another complex hardware development environment
  • Experience developing Basis of Estimates (BOEs) or supporting proposal, pricing, or Government contracting activities
  • Familiarity with FFP, CPFF, IDIQ, Delivery Order/CLIN structures, FAR cost principles, or Government proposal and pricing requirements
  • Working knowledge of hardware development activities such as prototype builds, EVT/DVT, verification, qualification, testing, and transition to production
  • Experience with NetSuite or similar ERP/financial systems, and/or PMP or a similar project management certification

US Salary Range

$111,500 – $156,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are considered part of Neros' total compensation package.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. We welcome all applicants without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

title: Composites Technician (De-tooling)
description:
At Layup Parts, we're developing the technology that will build the future.

We're a manufacturing technology company replacing months of lead time with days, using proprietary software, automation, and advanced manufacturing systems built for speed. Our customers are inventing what's next, in aerospace, defense, robotics, and beyond. To keep up with them, manufacturing has to change. That's what we're building.

The Composites Technician (De-Tooling) is responsible for safely and efficiently removing cured composite parts from molds, tools, and fixtures while protecting both the finished component and tooling from damage. This position plays an important role in maintaining production flow, part quality, and tool availability within the composites manufacturing process.

What You'll Do :

  • Perform de-tooling of cured composite parts from molds, tools, mandrels, and fixtures using approved work instructions and techniques.
  • Safely separate parts from tooling while minimizing the risk of damage to the part, mold, or associated tooling.
  • Use appropriate hand tools, pneumatic tools, wedges, lifting equipment, and other approved de-tooling equipment.
  • Identify appropriate release points and de-tooling sequences based on part and tool configuration.
  • Handle composite components carefully to prevent scratches, cracks, delamination, edge damage, or other defects.
  • Visually inspect parts and tooling during and after de-tooling and promptly identify potential defects or damage.
  • Clean tooling following part removal and prepare tools for subsequent production operations as required.
  • Assist with moving, lifting, and positioning molds, tools, and composite components using appropriate material-handling equipment.
  • Maintain organized work areas and properly store de-tooling tools and equipment.
  • Follow all safety requirements, including proper use of PPE and safe handling of sharp composite edges, tools, and equipment.
  • Communicate part, tool, or process issues to Production, Quality, or supervision before proceeding when requirements are unclear.
  • Support other composite manufacturing operations, including tool preparation, trimming, finishing, assembly, or general production support, as needed.

What We're Looking For:

  • Be awesome! Be the person you want to work with.
  • Previous experience in composites manufacturing, aerospace manufacturing, automotive, fabrication, machining, or another hands-on manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with composite molds, tooling, or de-tooling.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and comfort working with hand and pneumatic tools.
  • Ability to follow detailed written work instructions and established manufacturing processes.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to protecting product quality.
  • Ability to recognize when excessive force or an abnormal condition could damage a part or tool and stop work appropriately.
  • Ability to work independently after training while knowing when to escalate questions or concerns.
  • Strong reliability, organization, and communication skills.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to stand and work on the production floor for extended periods.
  • Ability to frequently bend, reach, push, pull, and perform repetitive hand movements.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds independently and heavier components with assistance or lifting equipment.
  • Ability to move metal parts that weigh 75-100 pounds into and out of ovens.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, pneumatic tools, and material-handling equipment.
  • Ability to wear required personal protective equipment, which may include safety glasses, gloves, hearing protection, and respiratory protection where applicable.

Equal Opportunity

Layup is an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, Veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law, including those with a criminal history, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the CA Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

title: Knowledge Management and Training Project Intern
description:
About Graphcore

Graphcore is a global leader in artificial intelligence computing systems. We design advanced semiconductors and data center hardware that provide the specialized processing power needed to advance AI while improving the efficiency required for broad adoption.

As part of SoftBank Group, Graphcore belongs to a family of companies developing transformative technologies. Our AI Engineering Campus in Austin supports the infrastructure used to develop and test the next generation of AI systems.

The Opportunity

As a Knowledge Management and Training Project Intern, you will help the Technical Services team develop and maintain clear documentation, training materials, and knowledge resources for data center engineering environments.

Working with engineers, operational teams, and subject matter experts, you will organize technical and operational information so that colleagues can find, understand, and apply current guidance. You will gain practical experience in documentation, onboarding, training content, knowledge systems, and project coordination with support from experienced team members.

What You Will Do

  • Create, review, and organize technical documentation, guidance, and standard operating procedures under the direction of Technical Services team members.
  • Help develop onboarding and training materials for engineers, technicians, and other colleagues who support data center engineering activities.
  • Work with subject matter experts to capture technical and operational information and translate it into clear, structured content.
  • Maintain and improve knowledge resources using approved collaboration and document-management tools.
  • Organize content so users can identify current guidance and locate the information they need efficiently.
  • Support the preparation of safety, compliance, and operational learning materials relevant to the team's work.

title: Product Designer
description:
At Superfeet, we’re Designed for movement. Built to change lives. That’s not just our mission, it’s the energy we bring to everything we do.

As Product Designer, you will lead product design for Superfeet product concepts, line extensions, and new product development. This is an individual contributor role (no current direct reports) and the primary internal design resource, guiding internal efforts and external contractors/partners as needed. You will partner closely with the product team and other key internal stakeholders to translate consumer insight, biomechanical intent, brand strategy, and commercial objectives into innovative, manufacturable solutions—owning design intent from concept through commercialization in support of Superfeet’s mission to keep athletes everywhere moving.

Our Product Designer will:
  • Own industrial design for assigned categories/projects from concept through production, aligning consumer/athlete needs, biomechanical intent, brand strategy, and business goals.
  • Push the boundaries of design language, form, function and materials while maintaining performance goals and developing manufacturability
  • Turn briefs, research, and market insight into clear concepts and product architecture that balance performance, comfort, durability, aesthetics, manufacturability, and cost.
  • Communicate design intent through sketches, CAD, renderings, prototypes, product specifications, and presentations to drive fast, aligned decisions.
  • Partner cross-functionally (across Product Management, Product Development, Engineering, Marketing, Operations) to iterate concepts/samples and deliver launch-ready solutions.
  • Support DFM, cost, and technical reviews—making smart tradeoffs without losing core design intent.
  • Manage external design/visualization partners as needed; contribute to innovation workstreams; model Superfeet values and build trusted relationships.
Your Skills & Abilities:
  • Strong design fundamentals and proficiency in sketching, prototyping, 3D CAD (Rhino preferred), rendering, Adobe Creative Suite, and technical communication.
  • Ability to translate athlete and consumer insights and performance requirements into compelling, manufacturable product concepts and design direction.
  • Strong functional problem-solving skills, including product architecture and line-building, with the ability to clearly articulate design decisions and rationale.
  • Knowledge of color, materials, finishes, manufacturing processes, construction, prototyping, tooling, and production considerations.
  • Ability to provide color, material, and finish direction and contribute to broader product and material strategies.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate across engineering, development, vendors, and manufacturing partners.
  • Strong organization and project management skills, including the ability to align teams, manage competing priorities, and deliver high-quality outcomes.
  • Passion for innovation, sport and movement, sustainable design, and creating products that positively impact people’s lives.

Your Qualifications:

  • People enjoy working with you
  • You have a Bachelor’s degree in Industrial/Product Design (or related)
  • +5 years designing and developing physical consumer products (sporting goods/footwear/performance preferred).
  • Proven experience owning products from initial concept through production.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering effectively with engineering, product development, vendors, and manufacturing teams.
  • Portfolio demonstrating functional problem-solving, product architecture and line-building, and thoughtful design rationale—not aesthetics alone.
  • Experience working with materials, finishes, manufacturing methods, prototyping, tooling, and production processes.

Compensation: $85,000.00 - $95,000.00 per year paid bi-weekly + Company & SMART Bonus opportunities

Location: Ferndale, WA 98248, WA (Open to hybrid with in-person time spent in Ferndale)

Why Join Superfeet Worldwide?

At Superfeet, we’re fueled by performance, innovation, and a mission to help athletes move better—from the ground up—ultimately making a positive impact in their lives. As a leader in the insole industry, we craft high-quality, performance-driven insoles that support movement at every level, from everyday activity to elite competitors.

We believe our employees are essential to that mission. We foster an inclusive, collaborative environment that encourages growth, sparks innovation, and challenges the status quo every step of the way.

We take care of our team with the same commitment we bring to every product we make: we go all in. title: Staff/Principal Product Manager
description:
BrightHire is a category-creating, high-growth, Series B software company with a mission to give everyone the hiring experience they deserve.

We deliver on this mission by transforming the way many of the world’s leading companies build exceptional teams. We created the Interview Intelligence category, and our clients include some of the world’s most innovative companies—Canva, OpenAI, Ramp, Hubspot—up to the Fortune 500.

The Role

We’re looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead some of BrightHire’s most consequential product initiatives, like major growth bets and new SKUs.

This is a high-judgment, hands-on role for an experienced leader. You’ll work across zero-to-one and scaling efforts: defining new AI-powered workflows, improving products used by hiring teams every day, and helping establish the product and technical foundations for BrightHire’s system of action for hiring.

You should be able to quickly understand the market and customer problems, separate the most impactful opportunities from the rest, conceive new solutions, and drive high-velocity, high-quality execution.

We’re also seeking someone who has personally built AI products – not simply worked adjacent to them. You understand model capabilities and limitations, prompts, evaluation, and the details that turn an AI prototype into a product customers trust and use with the right UX/UI and workflows.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead major product initiatives from customer discovery through launch, adoption, and iteration—including zero-to-one work in ambiguous, fast-moving areas.
  • Set a clear product direction and make high-quality prioritization decisions amid incomplete information.
  • Partner closely with Engineering and Design to build excellent AI products, getting hands-on with model behavior, prompts, context, human-in-the-loop design, evaluation, quality, and reliability.
  • Work directly with customers and prospects to validate problems and solutions, then turn insight into differentiated products.
  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Zoom teams to bring products to market and drive measurable customer value.
  • Define success metrics, use qualitative and quantitative signals to improve the product, and raise the bar for product judgment and AI craft across the team.

What You Bring

  • 7+ years of product management experience, ideally in B2B SaaS, AI, or high-growth environments.
  • Hands-on experience shipping generative AI products or agentic systems, including prompt and context design, evaluation, output quality, and user trust.
  • A track record of independently taking consequential products from early concept to successful customer adoption.
  • Strong product judgment: you can separate compelling AI demos from durable customer value and make difficult tradeoffs well.
  • Technical fluency and the ability to partner deeply with engineers on AI systems, quality, and reliability.
  • Exceptional customer instincts, with a high bar for craft, usability, and product quality.
  • Clear, influential communication across executives, technical teams, customers, and go-to-market partners.
  • Comfort operating with urgency and ambiguity while bringing clarity and focus to others.

Nice to have

  • Experience in recruiting, HR technology, workflow software, communications, or enterprise AI.
  • Experience building products that integrate with platforms such as ATSs, collaboration tools, or enterprise systems.
  • Experience working in a startup or leading zero-to-one products within a larger organization.

Why BrightHire

BrightHire is operating with the focus and customer intimacy of a category-defining product team, with the reach and advantages of Zoom behind us. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a major new product category, work directly with customers, and build products that can reach hiring teams at global scale.

You’ll join a team that cares deeply about the quality of the products we build and the experiences we create for candidates, hiring teams, and one another.

Compensation and Benefits

This role is eligible for Zoom’s compensation and benefits programs. The expected base salary range for this position is between $175,000 and $220,000 plus applicable bonus and equity opportunities. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, location, and job-related skills.

title: Software Engineering Manager
description:
Title: Software Engineering Manager

Location: Morrisville, NC

Anticipated Start Date: November 2026



About the Company:

NIRSense is a cardiology company focused on developing world-leading non-invasive medical devices. Our tools measure oxygenation changes in the body 10x deeper than typical pulse oximetry and track the electrophysiological activity of muscles and the brain. We are a growing team of technology developers seeking candidates interested in helping advance our capabilities for a wide range of interested stakeholders who are driven to transform the way humans understand and interact with their own health.



Job Summary:

The Software Engineering Manager will act as the people and technical lead for software across NIRSense's body-worn sensing devices, including embedded firmware, mobile and desktop applications, and the cloud backend. Key responsibilities include team management, project planning, and software lifecycle management under IEC 62304, with oversight of architecture, verification, release, and the implementation of algorithms developed by our biosensing scientists. The successful candidate will have shipped medical device software under IEC 62304 and knows how to keep a small team shipping compliant software reliably. This position will be located in Morrisville, NC and report directly to the Director of Operations.



Minimum Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional software development experience, including 3+ years managing software or firmware engineers.
  • Experience planning and executing concurrent software projects, including estimation and schedule management.
  • Experience improving established development practices, including code review, continuous integration, automated testing, and release management.
  • Software development experience in a regulated industry, medical device strongly preferred, with working knowledge of IEC 62304, ISO 13485, and 21 CFR Part 820 design controls.
  • Strong technical writing skills, including software plans, requirements, and verification records for the design history file.
  • Hands-on embedded C/C++ experience on resource-constrained, battery-powered microcontrollers, including firmware bring-up on new hardware.
  • Experience delivering BLE-connected devices with over-the-air updates, plus a companion mobile, desktop, or cloud application.
  • B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

description:

Nice to have:

  • Experience with electromechanical actuators, motors, gear trains, or precision mechanisms.

We are not just building components. We are reshaping the future of the Aerospace and Defense component industry, which is a $300B+ market! Come join us and help build next generation systems that will make a massive impact at global scale.

Responsible for ensuring suppliers meet ISI requirements for quality, service, delivery, and cost. Drive suppliers to continuously improve business and manufacturing processes. Lead these efforts without managerial guidance at several suppliers simultaneously.

  • DFM by engaging suppliers early in development cycle to feedback manufacturability improvements in the designs prior to production.

  • Demonstrable knowledge in evaluating and challenging supplier technical, quality, and business capabilities.
  • Demonstrable knowledge of a wide range of manufacturing processes including understanding of key input variables for quality, cost, and capacity.

Required Education and Training:

  • Minimum Education: BS degree in Engineering, advanced degree preferred.
  • Experience with statistical analysis software such as Minitab

title: Waterproofing Field Applicator
description:

About Blanchard Caulking & Coating

Blanchard Caulking & Coating (BCC) is a trusted provider of waterproofing, restoration, and specialty coating solutions. Our reputation is built on quality workmanship, attention to detail, clear communication, and a commitment to delivering exceptional results for our customers.

At BCC, we believe that teamwork is the foundation of our success. Our employees are the driving force behind our continued growth, and we take pride in creating an environment where hard work, accountability, craftsmanship, and professional growth are valued.

We are always looking for dedicated individuals who take pride in their work and want to build a long-term career with a company that prioritizes safety, quality, and teamwork.


Position Overview

Blanchard Caulking & Coating is seeking a dependable and motivated


Waterproofing Field Applicator to join our growing team.

The Waterproofing Field Applicator is responsible for performing high-quality waterproofing, caulking, coating, and restoration applications on commercial construction projects. This role requires strong attention to detail, a commitment to safety, and the ability to work effectively as part of a team while meeting project deadlines.


The ideal candidate has experience in waterproofing, construction, coatings, or related trades and takes pride in delivering quality workmanship. BCC provides opportunities for hands-on training, skill development, and career advancement for individuals who demonstrate commitment and a strong work ethic.


Key Responsibilities

  • Perform waterproofing applications including caulking, sealants, coatings, and deck coating systems.
  • Complete restoration work including tuck pointing, parking garage restoration, and related repair applications.
  • Apply coatings and waterproofing materials with precision to ensure long-term durability and water resistance.
  • Perform proper surface preparation including cleaning, masking, grinding, priming, and other required preparation procedures.
  • Identify and address potential issues including cracks, leaks, and surface deficiencies.
  • Safely operate equipment including forklifts, scissor lifts, ladders, and other specialized tools required for waterproofing applications.
  • Follow project specifications, safety procedures, and company standards.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and safe job sites throughout the duration of each project.
  • Communicate effectively with project supervisors and team members regarding job progress and project requirements.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of completed work when required.
  • Attend employee meetings and participate in company training opportunities.
  • Accept responsibility for the proper care, custody, and use of company equipment, tools, materials, and other company assets.


Qualifications & Requirements

  • Reliable, dependable, and punctual with a strong commitment to attendance and accountability.
  • Previous experience in waterproofing, caulking, coatings, restoration, or commercial construction preferred.
  • Experience with deck coatings, tuck pointing, and parking garage restoration is a plus.
  • Ability to safely operate construction equipment; certifications are a plus.
  • Understanding construction safety practices and job site requirements.
  • Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions.
  • Comfortable working at heights, on ladders, and in elevated work environments.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and perform physically demanding tasks.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Native Mobile
description:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer, Native Mobile to join the App Infra team within the Consumer & Business group and help lead Coinbase's greenfield native mobile app rewrite. This team is replacing the existing React Native app with native Swift and Kotlin builds, using AI-driven agentic workflows to translate and rebuild every core surface for millions of customers. Your direction will determine how the team works: you'll bring deep iOS or Android expertise to set the technical bar, own quality outcomes, and translate org strategy into the team's technical execution as product teams onboard to native.

What you'll do:

  • Own end-to-end architecture and delivery of core native app surfaces in Swift and Kotlin, operating at depth across the team's codebases and establishing the constrained architecture and compile-time boundaries that enforce strict quality standards.
  • Lead the agentic code translation workflow, implementing high-quality automated systems for the team's recurring migration work before asking for headcount, and setting what gets automated versus what stays human across the translation pipeline.
  • Own developer experience for the native codebase, accelerating every engineer who onboards by improving build speeds, local development workflows, and CI/CD reliability, and by defining the architectural patterns and documentation that make native mobile development at Coinbase a world-class experience.
  • Shape the dual-app agentic synchronization strategy during the transition, prioritizing the highest-impact outcomes and designing the daily agent automations and human review processes that keep native and React Native codebases in sync.
  • Become a leader throughout the entire mobile community at Coinbase, defining best practices, mentoring L3-L5 mobile engineers across all teams, and fostering connection and support between all mobile engineers.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 8+ years of iOS or Android mobile software engineering experience (Swift/iOS or Kotlin/Android), with working proficiency in the other platform and willingness to develop cross-platform fluency, as engineers on this team own both iOS and Android.
  • Track record of shipping high-quality mobile applications at scale with ownership of architecture decisions, performance budgets, and release quality, with outcomes that would not have happened without your direct involvement.
  • Deep understanding of mobile performance optimization, including cold start, frame stability, scroll jank, and time to interaction, with experience profiling and tuning across device tiers including low-end Android.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate org strategy into team-level technical execution, build alignment across cross-team and cross-functional partners, and secure commitment on migration timelines and quality standards.
  • Experience with AI-assisted code generation or LLM-driven development workflows, with demonstrated judgment on what to automate and what requires human review.
  • Experience improving developer experience through build systems, CI/CD pipelines, and release tooling, with improvements adopted beyond your immediate team.
  • Uses generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and measurable gains in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

title: Software Engineer III
description:
What you’ll be part of

Garner is on a mission to transform the U.S. healthcare system — and we’re the only proven player doing exactly that. We partner with employers to redesign how healthcare works: applying 550+ proprietary clinical metrics across 80+ specialties to a dataset of 320M+ patients to identify the best-performing doctors, then using compelling incentives to steer members to the care that helps them get healthier, faster.

The result is a rare “win win” — better care and lower costs for both members and employers. In just five years, our work has helped over 2.5 million people access higher-quality care and saved $1B in healthcare costs. We recently raised our Series E and have doubled five years running. If you've ever wanted your work to solve a problem that touches every person in this country, this is the opportunity to do exactly that. You'd be joining a team fundamentally reimagining healthcare in the U.S. — and using AI to scale that impact further and faster than anyone else can.

About the role:

We are seeking an exceptional Software Engineer III to join our Engineering team. Garner’s Engineering team tackles incredibly hard technical problems for a mission that truly matters. Our systems analyze billions of medical records to rank healthcare providers across the country. We are an AWS + Kubernetes shop, and we are constantly introducing new technologies as our system load doubles every year.   • Use AI to build, optimize, and maintain software systems
  • Collaborate across disciplines to understand our domain and iterate on projects

  • 2+ years of software engineering experience, especially with distributed event-driven architectures
  • A generalist software engineering mindset ready to learn new languages, frameworks, and techniques required for a fast paced startup environment
  • Familiarity with data security and HIPAA compliance
  • A desire to be a part of a high-performing, mission-driven team that operates with intense urgency, a strong sense of individual accountability, and a commitment to authentic feedback

What you’ll get here:

You’ll work on problems that matter, at a company working to change healthcare at scale. You’ll work at the intersection of AI and systemic healthcare reform, where the problems we solve are as interesting and compelling as the mission.

At Garner, you’ll take on real, ambitious problems with real ownership and autonomy, alongside exceptional, principles-based people who genuinely want you to win. It’s demanding by design. You’ll be challenged to stretch beyond what you thought possible and receive consistent coaching to help you grow and do the best work of your career. title: Senior Engineer, R&D Test Engineering
description:
About Us

We are Sila, a next-generation battery materials company. Our mission is to power the world’s transition to clean energy. To create this future, our team is building a better lithium-ion battery from the inside out today. We engineer and manufacture ground-breaking battery materials that significantly increase the energy density of batteries, while reducing their size and weight. The result? Smaller more powerful batteries that can unlock innovation in consumer devices and accelerate the mass adoption of electric cars to eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels. We're tackling one of the biggest challenges of our time every day, and together we're redefining what's possible. Are you ready to be a part of a team committed to changing the world?

Who You Are

We're seeking an experienced, hands-on R&D Test Engineer with an aptitude and desire for learning new things and making experiments happen. This position will put you at the forefront of Sila’s hardware and process development efforts, with a focus on leading, designing, executing, and analyzing experiments on lab and pilot scale equipment as part of a growing, dynamic test engineering team. Your experiments will deliver the critical data necessary to understand how equipment design, process conditions, and material structure interact, enabling data-informed decisions for scale-up.

You will strive to accelerate Sila’s pace of learning and drive the company towards impactful decisions. You work as a team: you will rely on engineers, scientists, and technicians who, in turn, rely on you. You work at the interface of material science, process engineering, equipment engineering, systems engineering, and data science. You turn raw data into critical insights. You run towards problems not away. If someone has an issue they need to debug, they come to you. You use your fundamental understanding, experiential insight, creative thinking, and the rest of the team to solve tough problems quickly and thoroughly. You have excellent communication skills and deftly navigate through technical discussions and debates.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Conduct complete R&D projects in collaboration with engineering teams, including test planning, experimental design, preparation, execution, analysis, and communication of results
  • Craft and execute effective experimental test plans
  • Find failure-modes, root-causes, and implement robust solutions
  • Provide critical insights through hands-on experience, deep process knowledge of the equipment, and thorough analysis of experimental data, system logs, and observations.
  • Manage test platforms. Strive to make them world class.
  • Formulate, lead, and facilitate complex data analysis projects

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

  • Exceptional laboratory testing aptitude. Intuition for what will work and ability to execute quickly and effectively
  • Experience conducting or leading experimental R&D projects
  • Demonstrated experience with complex reactive or thermo-mechanical systems like reactors, generators, catalytic systems, flow cells, or similar machines/processes
  • Understanding and proven application of mechanical, process, and materials engineering principles: heat, flow, structures, thermodynamics, kinetics, and materials.
  • Experience with data analysis and sufficient language knowledge, or polyglotism, to navigate data platforms in Python
  • Experience with developing and deploying new instrumentation and measurement systems
  • Demonstrated experience in electronics, wiring, and instrumentation (analog signals, AC and DC power fundamentals, control wiring, and diagnostic tools) and experience implementing lab or field-deployed electronics, sensors, and actuators
  • At least a B.S. in engineering or physical sciences (e.g. Mechanical Engineering, Physics, etc.), advanced degrees preferred.
  • 4+ years of relevant professional experience; an advanced degree (e.g., MS, ME) may substitute for a portion of the required experience.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

  • Pass a respirator fit test and be able to wear respiratory protection on a daily basis
  • Wear personal protective equipment including, but not limited to, a lab coat, gloves, safety glasses, and steel toe safety shoes
  • Move items up to 50 lbs with the assistance of lift equipment and carts
  • Move long distances (such as from building to building) and be stationary for extended periods of time
  • Reach low shelves or items on the floor
  • Precise and repetitive handling of a range of material quantities
  • Operate a computer and other office equipment, such as a laptop, copier/printer, etc in a fixed location

The starting base pay for this role is between $128,000 and $162,000 at the time of posting. The actual base pay depends on many factors, such as education, experience, and skills. Base pay is only one part of Sila’s competitive Total Rewards package that can include benefits, perks, equity, and bonuses. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

title: Senior Manager, Security Operations Center
description:
About the team:

The Information Security organization advances the overall state of security at Rubrik through critical initiatives and coordination of large security projects. Information Security builds technologies, tools, and processes to better enable teams at Rubrik to develop secure software and protect data and systems with appropriate security controls. Information Security also develops systems to monitor and respond to attacks against our assets, provides awareness education to teams on security best practices for data protection, and ensures data governance and data sharing relationships with third parties in order to securely protect Rubrik information.

About the role:

Rubrik is hiring a Senior Manager to lead our Security Operations Center, including our FedRAMP-authorized environment. Incident response sits at the core of what the SOC does, alongside detection and monitoring, and this role owns all of it. You'll inherit a SOC that has already grown a lot in scale and maturity, and your job is to take it further: stronger detection and incident response, broader coverage as our environment gets more complex, and a real strategy for AI in the SOC.

Driving our AI SOC transformation is a core part of this role. You'll be the one setting the strategy for how AI enables the SOC: scaling coverage beyond what headcount alone could support, reducing alert fatigue on L1 analysts, and giving analysts more room to focus on complex investigations and incident response.

You'll also own SOC leadership for our FedRAMP environment: same detection, incident response, and operational rigor, applied to the teams and processes inside that compliance boundary.

What you'll do:

Team Leadership & Development-

  • Hire, train, mentor, and evaluate SOC analysts across both commercial and FedRAMP-scoped teams.
  • Build a culture of collaboration, ownership, and continuous learning within the SOC.
  • Keep an eye on signal quality and analyst experience so analysts are working real alerts, not chasing noise.
  • Develop career paths, training programs, and succession planning for SOC analysts.

Monitoring & Incident Response-

  • Direct 24/7 monitoring and make sure coverage stays consistent across shifts and regions.
  • Serve as Incident Manager for major security incidents, leading the response and collaborating across InfoSec teams as needed during investigations.
  • Drive continuous improvement of SOC processes, including incident response playbooks, runbooks, and escalation procedures.
  • Make sure incident response processes hold up to the extra rigor FedRAMP requires.

AI SOC Strategy & Tooling-

  • Own the roadmap for AI-enabled SOC capabilities: AI-assisted triage, investigation support, response automation.
  • Deploy AI/ML and automation to cut down L1 toil and alert fatigue, so analysts spend more time on complex investigations.
  • Work with Threat Operations and Security Engineering to evaluate, pilot, and roll out AI SOC tools.
  • Enable the safe use of AI tools internally, while building the SOC's ability to detect and defend against AI-enabled threat actors.

Detection Tuning & Coverage Expansion-

  • Partner with Threat Operations to grow detection maturity and expand coverage as the Rubrik environment grows (cloud, SaaS, on-prem, and FedRAMP systems).
  • Work with Threat Operations to close detection gaps, cut false positives, and keep detections aligned to current threat intel and MITRE ATT&CK.
  • Feed incident findings back to Threat Operations to drive continuous improvement of detection logic.
  • Close the loop with Security Engineering to bring in additional logging based on incident and investigation data.

Strategy & Operations Management-

  • Set the direction and operating model for a modern SOC.
  • Own planning, budgeting, staffing, and resource allocation, including for the FedRAMP-scoped team.
  • Track and report on key metrics like MTTD (mean time to detect) and MTTR (mean time to respond), analyst workload, and detection coverage.
  • Keep evolving the operating model as the company scales.

Tool & Technology Evaluation-

  • Make the strategic calls on SIEM/SOAR platforms and automation.
  • Own the SOC's technology roadmap, including build-vs-buy decisions, vendor evaluation, and integration with the broader security stack.

Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Communication-

  • Give the CISO and executive leadership regular updates on security posture, SOC performance, and notable threats.
  • Represent the SOC in cross-functional and executive settings, translating technical detail into business risk.

Compliance & Audits-

  • Support FedRAMP and other security audits: evidence collection, control validation, remediation tracking for the SOC's scope.
  • Build and maintain compliance and operational hygiene reporting for both commercial and FedRAMP environments.
  • Make sure SOC processes and documentation hold up to regulatory and contractual requirements.

Experience you'll need:

  • 8+ years in security operations, incident response, or a related field, including prior experience leading a SOC, incident response included, in a management or senior lead role.
  • Experience serving as an Incident Manager, leading incident investigations and coordinating across teams under pressure.
  • Experience building or maturing a SOC operating model: 24/7 coverage, playbooks, escalation processes.
  • Hands-on background in detection and response, with real fluency in SIEM/SOAR platforms and common attacker tactics and techniques (MITRE ATT&CK).
  • Experience managing and developing SOC analysts, including hiring, mentoring, and performance management.
  • A track record of defining and reporting SOC metrics (MTTD, MTTR, coverage, etc.) to both technical and executive audiences.
  • Experience supporting compliance frameworks and audits (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar). Direct FedRAMP experience is a strong plus.
  • Strong communication skills and comfort briefing executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders on posture and incidents.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen, as required for FedRAMP responsibilities.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Direct experience evaluating, piloting, or rolling out AI/ML-driven security tooling: AI-assisted triage, automated investigation, GenAI copilots for SOC work, and similar.
  • Experience operating within or leading a FedRAMP-authorized security function.
  • Comfort with cloud-native and SaaS environments in addition to traditional on-prem infrastructure.
  • Certifications like GCIH, GCFA, CISSP, or CISM are a plus.

What Success Looks Like-

  • Detection and response keep maturing while coverage expands across a growing environment.
  • Alert fatigue and manual triage on L1 analysts drop, thanks to real AI SOC tooling adoption.
  • MTTD/MTTR trends improve, and analyst retention and satisfaction go up with them.
  • FedRAMP SOC operations stay clean and audit-ready, with no material findings tied to SOC process gaps.
  • A strong bench of SOC analysts, with a clear path for future leaders to grow into.

title: Software Engineer 3
description:
The Application Modernization Platform (AMP) team is dedicated to solving one of the industry's biggest challenges: transforming rigid, legacy applications that suffer from poor scalability and high operating costs into modern, microservices-based architectures on MongoDB. To accelerate this transition, MongoDB is building a dedicated Platform and Infrastructure team to develop the Application Modernisation Platform and Infrastructure . As we help customers modernize their application and data ecosystems, we face the challenge of deploying complex tooling into highly restrictive client environments and architecting automated verification frameworks to ensure data equivalence.

This new team will architect the platform foundation and infrastructure that enables a "build once, run anywhere" model, ensuring our AI-powered modernisation suite operates seamlessly regardless of a client's security or network constraints. We are looking for engineers to join this high-visibility initiative, where you will solve unique distributed systems puzzles and help shape the future of how global enterprises leverage data and AI.

We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer who thrives on solving infrastructure constraints and building developer-centric modernisation platforms with a strong background in building software testkits/frameworks. The ideal candidate will be designing and building automated frameworks that validate functional equivalence, performance benchmarks, and data integrity. From leveraging LLMs for unit test generation to building contract testing frameworks, your work will be the safety net for the world’s largest enterprise migrations.

This role will be based in our India office in Gurgaon and offers a hybrid working model.

The ideal candidate for this role will have

  • 3-4 years of commercial software development experience with at least one JVM language such as Java, preferably using the Spring ecosystem
  • Expertise integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into the developer workflow to automate unit test generation and edge-case discovery
  • Experience building developer tools, infrastructure, or complex testing frameworks
  • Solid experience in software architecture and development
  • Deep expertise in application/database modernization with proven ability to design and implement frameworks that ensure database state equivalence across different implementations
  • Must understand change data capture, event-driven database interception (MongoDB listeners, RDBMS triggers), and state comparison algorithms with pattern-based exclusions. Strong Spring Boot (or equivalent Java framework), MongoDB (or equivalent), and JDBC/JPA skills required
  • Extensive experience with relational and document data modeling and hands-on experience with at least one SQL database (Postgres, MySQL, etc) and at least one document database (e.g. MongoDB)
  • Good understanding of algorithms, data structures and their time and space complexity
  • Curiosity, a positive attitude, and a drive to continue learning
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Position Expectations

  • Contribute high-quality, well-tested code to the modernization and framework team and its surrounding services
  • Collaborate effectively with Product Management, other engineers, and designers to build and deliver on the product roadmap
  • Participate actively in code reviews to enforce best practices and patterns
  • Help troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues in our distributed systems
  • Give and solicit feedback on technical design documents and pull requests
  • Perform tasks related to process such as CI/CD, quality, testing, etc

Success Measures

Within the first three months, you will have:

  • Familiarize yourself with the MongoDB Modernization Infrastructure & Frameworks stack
  • Set up software development infrastructure (tech stack, build tools, etc) to enable development using the relevant tech stacks
  • Started collaborating with your peers and contributed to code reviews and design reviews

Within six months, you will have:

  • Familiarised yourself with the rest of our the application modernization tool stack
  • Delivered at least one large scale feature that spans the entire tech stack
  • Reviewed and contributed to scope and technical design documents

Within 12 months, you will have:

  • Become a key contributor to our stack, capable of taking on complex features independently
  • Helped recruit and interview new members of the team

title: Spring 2027 Museum Education (Paid) Intern
company: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
location: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
description:
Internship: Museum Education (Paid)


For application deadlines and internship dates, please visit: .


Museum Overview: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the “Smithsonian of country music,” celebrated for its broad cultural impact, educational mission, and unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts. Chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964, the Museum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, educational organization that documents and interprets the history of country music. The Museum collects objects and archival materials that illustrate the evolving history and traditions of country music and provides diverse learning opportunities through educational programs, publications, and exhibitions.


First opened in 1967 on Nashville’s Music Row, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum launched its current downtown location in 2001. In 2014, the Museum unveiled a $100 million expansion that doubled its footprint. The Museum now encompasses 350,000 square feet of exhibition galleries, archival storage, retail stores, and event space. The Museum owns Hatch Show Print, a letterpress print shop opened in 1879, and it operates Historic RCA Studio B, where Dolly Parton, Elvis Presley, and many others recorded. In addition, the Museum offers the Taylor Swift Education Center for students, teachers, and families, and dedicated performance spaces in the CMA Theater and Ford Theater, both of which regularly host nationally recognized live music and cultural events.


In 2024, the Museum was awarded the prestigious National Medal of Arts by President Joe Biden. The medal is the highest award given to artists and arts institutions by the United States government. The White House Citation, which accompanied the medal, recognized the Museum’s work, which “preserves history, honors giants of the genre, and inspires future generations to write their own songs about the American story.”


Internship Program Overview: The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum offers paid internships to full-time college students (undergraduate and graduate) that advance the educational goals of the intern and help to promote the Museum’s mission. The Museum’s internship program offers work-based learning opportunities that introduce college students to museum-related careers and other professions found in large cultural organizations. Internships are designed for a maximum commitment of 25 hours per week for 12 weeks with consideration given to individual university requirements. Additional adjustments to the 12-week, 25-hour schedule will be at the discretion of the internship supervisor. Educational programs which operate on a quarterly basis may be accommodated. Motivated students who are seeking hands-on experiences in a team-oriented environment will find excellent opportunities at the Museum.

The application process for prospective interns includes the submission of:

  • An online application for the specific internship you are applying for via our internal hiring system
  • A resume
  • A one-page cover letter; it is recommended that your cover letter explain how your education and experience will contribute positively to this internship and how this internship relates to your academic pursuits and/or career goals

What We Offer Interns:

  • The hourly rate for this position is $15/hr. for students pursuing a bachelor's degree; $18/hr. for students pursuing a master's degree or higher
  • Free 24/7 downtown parking or WeGo bus pass
  • Complimentary admission to the Museum for yourself
  • Two complimentary Museum admission passes for friends and family use
  • Free guided tour of Hatch Show Print, Historic RCA Studio B, and the Museum’s galleries
  • Discounts at Museum stores and restaurants
  • Free or discounted entry to local venues including: National Museum of African American Music, the Opry, Ryman Auditorium, and more!
  • Fun, friendly, and supportive learning environment

Field Forward Stipend: Field Forward is a living and relocation stipend, offered to select candidates in addition to the paid internship, that supports students who identify as traditionally underrepresented in cultural arts careers and students with demonstrated financial need. Field Forward’s goals are to encourage diverse student engagement with the Museum and the broader museum field and to promote educational and professional experience and training to students historically underrepresented in museum and other cultural arts professions. Students must submit an additional application and demonstrate financial need (if applicable) to be considered. To learn more, including important deadlines, please visit: .


Departmental Overview: Charged with the mission of educating varied audiences about country music, the Education and Community Engagement Department develops programs and resources that illuminate the stories, themes, and music explored in the Museum’s galleries. Serving nearly 100,000 people per year through 1,100 programs, the Education and Community Engagement Department supports students of all ages, from school groups and families who engage in hands-on learning activities to general Museum guests who experience performance presentations during their visit. A creative and curious team, staff is composed of traditional and nontraditional educators, including classroom teachers, visual artists, historians, Museum educators, and professional musicians. Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum educators share a passion for country music, popular culture, and lifelong learning and regularly collaborate to develop and implement dynamic educational offerings commensurate with one of the most-visited history museums in America.


Museum Education Internship Overview: The Museum Education internship is designed for a commitment of 25 hours per week for a minimum of 12 weeks, flexible within Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. CST. This internship's goal is to engage in a variety of interdisciplinary educational experiences in a museum environment through the School Programs department.

School Programs provide dynamic, interdisciplinary learning experiences that support curriculum standards in core subject areas, such STEAM, College and Career Readiness, English Language Arts, Social Studies, Social and Emotional Learning, and fine arts curriculum for grades pre-K–12.

The Museum Education intern will receive hands-on training from Museum educators, and they will interact directly with student and teacher audiences. The intern will assist with program delivery and facilitation, support program preparations, facilitate administrative tasks, support evaluation and assessment, attend team meetings, and research and develop resources to support programming.


Specific Internship Duties:

  • Assist the School Programs manager in daily activities such as preparing and facilitating student programs in the Museum galleries and classrooms
  • Set specific, personal goals and work with the School Programs manager to achieve them
  • Develop and practice interdepartmental communication skills and general professionalism
  • Perform administrative tasks as needed

title: Senior Development Engineer
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

ABOUT ENGINEERING AT ROCKET LAB:

Engineering is the heart of Rocket Lab. We build world-class rockets and spacecraft and we launch them, often.

As a Senior Development Engineer in Propulsion, you'll own what powers Electron to orbit: Engines, turbopumps, valves, injectors, and the fluid systems that feed them.

First sketch to flight-ready hardware, and the standard everyone else builds to. You'll define the requirements, iterate in NX with analysis and manufacturing, own the EBOM, and release the drawings that get parts built. Then you'll plan and run the campaign that proves it, component rigs to hot fire, and coach the engineers who'll run the next one. Once it's flying, you define how it's operated and maintained.

It's hands-on, fast-paced problem solving where rapid innovation meets the highest safety standards and your hardware launches.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

  • Technical standard -You define best practice, consistently pick the right solution, and coach the team to the same bar
  • Manage Risk -You see it before it happens, put the mitigation in place, and check it held
  • Unsolved problems -When something stalls between teams or falls outside anyone's process, you take it, unasked, and bring others up as you go
  • Planning -Department level plans, work distributed across the team, and the new processes and equipment that make the next engine faster than the last
  • Judgement -You're the technical tiebreaker. The deciding argument is always what's best for the company
  • The people around you -You run meetings that go somewhere, convey technical information concisely enough to change direction, and deputise for the lead when needed

Some days you're deep in test data. Others you're on the production floor, taking hard feedback from the technicians who build your parts or in the development lab, pushing a new concept or a flight-ready engine to its limits. Both are good days. This is not a desk job.

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 6+ year’s industry experience and an engineering degree.
  • Deep manufacturing and production understanding.
  • Experience taking a product from development into rate production.
  • Proven ability to technically steer a team across multiple engineering projects, concept through to operation, not one project, several.
  • Depth in at least two of these:
  • Skills that transfer. You don't need to have built a rocket. You need to have solved hard engineering problems well enough that the domain is the only new thing.
  • Structural: Will it hold up under load?
  • Vibration - How does it shake and resonate?
  • CFD - How do fluids and gases flow through it?
  • Thermal - How does heat move through it?
  • Fatigue and creep - Will it wear out or deform over time?
  • FMEA - What could go wrong, before it does?
  • Root cause - Why did it fail, and how do we stop it happening again?

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Master's or PhD
  • Rocket, aerospace or automotive background
  • Applied analysis - structural, modal, CFD, thermal, fatigue, DFMEA/PFMEA or DMAIC
  • Experience with our toolset - NX, Teamcenter, JAMA and Jira. If you've used the equivalents, you'll pick these up fast

If the above sounds like you apply now!

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

title: Spacecraft Thermal Engineer I
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SPACECRAFT THERMAL ENGINEER I

Based out of Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Spacecraft Thermal Engineer I is responsible for overseeing the thermal design, analysis, testing, and validation of Rocket Lab’s space vehicles. You’ll be expected to perform thermal modeling and data analysis while working closely with the test and design engineers to capture the vehicle’s thermal performance and provide input for design improvements. You will support the Space Systems organization, with deliverables required for internal leadership, board of directors, and investors.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

  • Complete thermal modeling and analysis of vehicles
  • Conduct thermal design trade studies that successfully balance performance margins, resource use, risk, cost, and schedule
  • Identify and resolve thermal design, acceptance, and performance issues for space vehicle components and assemblies
  • Design and execute thermal tests for space vehicle components and assemblies
  • Perform thermal model validation using test and in-flight data
  • Liaise with all levels of program and engineering staff on thermal design and test matters, and support other teams/disciplines as necessary
  • Identify and research potential vendors of thermal control materials

QUALIFICATIONS YOU BRING AS THERMAL ENGINEER I

  • Bachelor’s degree in aerospace or mechanical engineering; or other engineering degree
  • Thermal engineering experience
  • U.S citizenship is required, due to program requirements

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Master's or PhD in aerospace or mechanical engineering; or other engineering degree
  • Strong background in heat transfer
  • Experience with thermal systems and passive thermal management techniques
  • Familiarity using Siemens NX and Teamcenter, with emphasis on model interrogation and defeaturing for subsequent analyses
  • Demonstrated experience with Thermal Desktop
  • Experience with planning, execution, and data analysis of thermal balance tests
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Ability to work independently but also build strong working relationships with colleagues
  • Experience with constant conductance and variable conductance heat pipes
  • Experience working with multi-layer insulation: design, fabrication, installation, and test
  • Experience with 0-D and 1-D thermal/fluid networks
  • Familiarity with scripting languages such as Python and MATLAB
  • Familiarity with thermal engineering tools such as NX Space Systems Thermal, ANSYS, SINDA, and THERMICA
  • Knowledge of aspects of launch and on-orbit operations
  • Familiarity with orbital mechanics and attitude dynamics related to thermal analysis

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

$90,150—$126,425 USD

$83,200—$114,400 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

We also develop the scalable platforms and capabilities that power these solutions, enabling faster innovation, support for evolving measurement methodologies, and integration with Pinterest’s broader ads, data, and experimentation ecosystems. title: Production Operations Internship (Summer 2027)
description:
Amca is building America’s new industrial base. Since the 1990s, our ability to build new aviation and military systems and maintain the ones we already have has eroded. Today, the gap between what the nation needs to produce and what it is capable of producing is the largest it has been in generations.

To help close that gap, Amca rapidly develops and manufactures new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. Today, we operate seven factories nationwide, including our advanced prototyping and testing headquarters in El Segundo, and deliver avionics, hydraulic, and electrical components for platforms such as the F-35, F-16, F/A-18, 737MAX, 787, A320neo, A321, Mk-48, and M1 Abrams.

Overview:

Amca is hiring hands-on production operations interns to help keep tens of thousands of components a month moving through the factories quickly, efficiently, and reliably. The work also supports Protoshop, where the goal is to take new engineered products from design to qualification faster than any other organization in the country.

Interns spend significant time on the floor, machining, testing, and assembling parts, and use what they learn firsthand to make those processes better. The best ideas come from the people doing the work, and improvements show up in output, lead times, and quality. All interns should want to get their hands dirty.

Responsibilities:

  • Work hands-on in machining, assembly, and test, learning how each part is actually made and where the process breaks down
  • Spot bottlenecks, rework, and wasted motion from the floor, then work with operators and engineers to fix them
  • Support Protoshop programs as new products move from design through build, testing, and qualification
  • Develop and document standard work, fixtures, tooling, and process improvements that make production faster and more repeatable
  • Track throughput, cycle time, yield, and scrap to confirm that changes are working
  • Coordinate with engineering, supply chain, quality, and program management to keep builds on schedule

title: Supply Chain Planner
description:
At Smiths Detection, we are looking for a driven and analytical Supply Chain Planner to support our manufacturing operations by ensuring the right materials are available at the right time to meet customer demand. This role will work closely with Procurement, Production, Logistics and Suppliers to manage material flow, optimize inventory levels and support production continuity in a dynamic manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute MRP planning activities within SAP/ERP systems and take appropriate actions on rescheduling, pull-ins and push-outs.
  • Monitor material availability, stock levels and supply commitments to support production requirements.
  • Manage Purchase Requisitions (PRs) and monitor Purchase Orders (POs) to ensure timely delivery.
  • Conduct demand versus supply analysis and proactively identify and mitigate material shortages.
  • Develop and maintain production schedules while considering material readiness and capacity constraints.
  • Drive material recovery plans and expedite critical deliveries to minimize production disruptions.
  • Monitor inventory health, including safety stock, MOQ, excess, obsolete and ageing inventory.
  • Analyze supplier performance and collaborate with vendors on delivery recovery and lead-time improvements.
  • Generate planning reports and insights using Excel and other analytical tools to support decision-making.
  • Work cross-functionally to improve planning accuracy, inventory optimization and on-time delivery performance.

What You'll Bring

The ideal candidate will possess:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or a related discipline. Diploma holders with strong relevant supply chain planning experience may also be considered.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in Supply Chain Planning, Material Planning, Production Planning, Purchasing, Inventory Management, or a related manufacturing environment.
  • Hands-on experience using SAP ERP or other ERP systems for planning, inventory management, Purchase Requisitions (PR), Purchase Orders (PO), and Material Requirements Planning (MRP).
  • Strong understanding of MRP, MPS, demand planning, inventory control, material planning, and production planning principles.
  • Proven ability to perform demand versus supply analysis, shortage management, recovery planning, and supplier delivery follow-up activities.
  • Experience managing supplier commitments, inventory optimization, inventory reduction initiatives, and obsolescence avoidance.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including data analysis, Pivot Tables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, and planning reports.
  • Exposure to Power BI, Power Query, or other data analytics and reporting tools is advantageous.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Self-motivated team player with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across functions and take ownership of achieving challenging operational targets.

We offer…

Join us and we’ll help build your career, with excellent training and opportunities for career growth across the business, both locally and globally. You’ll experience an inclusive environment, with strong leadership and a focus on safety and wellbeing. You’ll also have the flexibility to choose from a wide range of benefits to suit your lifestyle, offering you and your family support from a health and wellbeing, financial and lifestyle perspective.
